brief.todays_call: Feeds thin into Eid-ul-Azha — Brent last at $94.11, $17 off the May $111 peak, ~$680M/month of import-bill relief. The IMF’s new 3-year programme imposes recapitalization timelines the banking system has deferred at 35.73% NPL. Government borrowing crossed the annual target in nine months — the sovereign funding bank rescues is itself overdrawn. The book stays flat through the Eid gap — bank the crude tailwind, defer directional bets to post-Eid resumption.

sections.tldr: Both prints held from Q4 2025; IMF conditionality reshapes recapitalization clock.
sections.analysis: NPL at 35.73% and CAR at 1.56% — both Q4 2025 prints, held pending Q1 disclosure. The IMF agreement on a new 3-year reform programme shifts the structural calculus: conditionality will almost certainly include recapitalization targets and NPL resolution timelines that the system has deferred since the crisis deepened. Government bank borrowing crossing the annual target in nine months compounds the pressure — the sovereign balance sheet that would fund bank rescues is itself under fiscal strain. The binding constraint remains circular: the fiscal authority must recapitalize banks it cannot afford to recapitalize while borrowing from the very banking system it needs to rescue. Zero duration on bank paper until Q1 data prints and IMF conditionality terms clarify.

sections.tldr: Borrowing exceeds target in 9 months; budget June 7 the next catalyst.
sections.analysis: Government bank borrowing at BDT 0.92tn — crossing the annual target in nine months confirms fiscal financing running ahead of plan. The IMF agreement on a new 3-year reform programme provides the external financing lifeline but introduces conditionality constraining FY27 budget flexibility on both revenue and expenditure. ADB’s upgraded $5B commitment over five years adds project-level depth but does not address the recurrent fiscal gap. The binding constraint: fiscal consolidation conditionality arrives while credit growth sits at 6.03% and NPL at 35.73% — the sovereign that must fund bank recapitalization is itself borrowing beyond plan. Budget June 7 is the decision point.

sections.verdict: Brent last at $94.11 — feeds dark for Eid; $17 off the $111 peak extends ~$680M/month of import-bill relief into the break.
sections.tldr: Commodity feeds dark for Eid; Brent last traded at $94.11.
sections.analysis: Commodity feeds dark into Eid-ul-Azha — Brent last traded at $94.11, WTI at $90.55, Brent-WTI spread compressed to $3.56. The cumulative $17 decline from the $111 May peak represents ~$680M/month of import-bill relief, partially neutralizing reserves pressure from ACU settlements. The decline has been demand-driven, not supply normalization — signaling global slowdown risk alongside the import-bill tailwind. For Bangladesh, the risk sits on the export side: crude declining at this velocity typically leads global demand by 2–3 months, and garment orders are exposed. Treasury desks should bank the import-bill gain and model $85–95 for H2 rather than extrapolating further decline. Post-Eid resumption will test whether $90 is a floor or a waypoint.
